Edwin Sodi

By: Harri Vithi | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
A serial tenderpreneur with a penchant for incomplete projects.

Unique Selling Point:
Edwin Sodi is a controversial tenderpreneur with questionable links to ANC politicians, including SA’s number two citizen - Paul Mashatile. In the past 10 years, Sodi's companies have been awarded over R 2 billion in tenders and counting across the country North West, Free State, Eastern Cape, Limpopo and Gauteng.


Summary:
Three day shoot - three main focus projects:-

Free State Bucket Eradication Project - R 275 million this ties in with Rooiwal as the Senekal wastewater treatment plant remains incomplete and untreated raw sewage flows through the streets. Sodi’s former friend Selloane Lephoi worked with him at Total South Africa where he was in HR recruitment. Ironically, she is now a community activist and one of the incomplete projects she has been raising the alarm on happens to be Sodi’s. Lephoi says Edwin was such a great human being, she knew his first wife and he was her plus one when she didn’t want to be “dateless”. Lephoi says she was shocked when she saw Sodi at the Zondo Commission as they lost touch years ago.

Raising of the Tzaneen Dam Wall - value as yet unknown, water projects are the biggest tenders available in provinces. The SIU found the tender was awarded irregularly as it was on a “urgent basis” but there was no urgency as a decision had been taken to raise the wall in 2011. Sodi is from Bolobedu, Limpopo and is alleged to have built his own “Nkandla” there. Therefore, it represents an opportunity to film links in his village - Matipane

Barcelona Primary School - Community members in Etwatwa, Benoni have been protesting and demanding a proper school since 1996. It’s unclear how many contractors have been awarded a tender to build the school in the last 20 years but reportedly, in July 2018, Edwin’s Sodi - Blackhead Consulting was awarded a tender of over R 10 million to build the school. It’s unclear how much of the R 10 million was paid or what went wrong but to date the land upon which the school was to be built remains vacant.



Ficksburg Bucket Toilet Eradication Project - Expenditure to date R 87 million

“Where water should be flowing, it isn’t. Where sewage shouldn’t be flowing, it is.”

Scene 1:
Out of focus shot of a beautiful high end bar, cocktail music playing in the background - a bar tender opening a bottle of champagne comes into focus - the presenter walks into shot and stands by the bar

Link:
Champagne colloquially referred to as champopo represents the finer things in life - for most, it takes long hours, smart work and sacrifice to live a life of luxury but for some perhaps all it takes is an incomplete tender

Viz: Bartender pours champagne into glass transition to sewage flowing through streets of Ficksburg

Scene 2:
An old lady wakes up in the morning, begins to clean up, grabs a bucket (we don’t see the contents)..we track her as she walks to the “toilet” and enters, closing the door behind her. She emerges with the bucket and returns to her home, washes her hands and sits down

Parallel scene, a young child walks across the road into a “toilet” closes the door and emerges…inside is a precarious drop hole which exposes the child to daily risk

Scene 3:
Selloane Lephoi driving through Senekal pointing out the raw sewage flowing through the streets…she paints a picture of what type of area Senekal is - according to her the type of forgotten area on the outskirts often abused by ANC officials to secure tenders and not fulfill them

Who is Selloane Lephoi

Selloane is a Setsoto Service Delivery Forum (SSDF) political party leader. Selloane’s home town, Ficksburg, is on the border with Lesotho. Ficksburg is the murder capital of the Free State province and Selloane says this is because it’s the entry point for Zama-Zamas who make shady deals with municipal officials. Selloane left her high-powered job as a consultant in Johannesburg - at first believing she would take a three month hiatus. However, she says the issues in her hometown drew her in and she began educating community members about the lies the local mayor was peddling. The Senekal Wastewater treatment plant is one of may corrupt projects Selloane has exposed. She has reported the matter to the Hawks and says it’s finally receiving genuine attention.

According to Selloane, the first phase of the water and sanitation project was run by the municipality for a year then Edwin Sodi’s G5 Group took over. The municipality had negotiated and concluded contracts with the workers which Sodi allegedly honored for 3 months before approaching the municipality and brokering a deal tro half their wages. In order to facilitate this, the workers were transferred to EPWP contracts. Despite having their wages, Selloane says Sodi continues to claim their full salaries in G5 Group’s invoicing - pocketing the rest. It’s important to note Sodi has resigned as director of G5 Group but workers allege he visits the sit on occasion raising questions whether Sodi merely resigned on paper.

Like Hammanskraal and the Rooiwal Wastewater Treatment Plant, raw sewage has entered the community’s water source increasing the risk of a Cholera outbreak. Selloane says the human waste which flows into the Caledon River will eventually make its way into tributaries which link to Johannesburg water sources (will need to confirm this)

Selloane will take us to the sites and different homes and schools where she says sewage readily flows.

Parys Correctional Services - R 282 million

While in the Free State, we will drive 2 hours to Parys Correctional Services - where there’s a R 282 million project secured by NJR Projects/G5 Projects. Yet another project Sodi failed ot deliver on.

Raising of the Tzaneen Dam Wall - R 600 million

VIZ:
Presenter walking on the dam wall

In November 2015, Lepelle Northern Water awarded Edwin Sodi’s - Blackhead Consulting- a tender to raise the Tzaneen Dam Wall value as yet unknown. The Special Investigations Unit found that:

The SCM process followed in the appointment of Blackhead Consulting (Pty) Ltd was not compliant with Section 217 of the Constitution in that the process was not fair, equitable, transparent, competitive and cost effective.

LNW did not follow their SCM processes in appointing the service provider.

There was no emergency/ urgency in the appointment of the service provider for the Raising of the Tzaneen dam wall. LNW was supposed to have gone out on a normal competitive SCM process. The project was part of the Department's planning approved in 2012.

The SIU is also investigating alleged kickbacks to an official in order to “smooth” the deal.
The SIU says it is not in a position to discuss ongoing investigations.

I am in the process of securing a community activist to detail the impact of the incomplete dam wall. Ward Councillors say they have been instructed not to speak with the media about the dam.

“A budget of R209-million exists for raising the wall of Limpopo’s Tzaneen Dam. The department had to take the project over from Lepelle Northern Water,a subsidiary of the water department that has been mired in corruption, especially because of its failure to get water to people in Giyani.
A “loss of public confidence” and a number of cost overruns and contractual irregularities have resulted in the Tzaneen project being years behind schedule.
To solve these delays, the department said it has referred companies to the Special Investigating Unit (SIU) and other arms of government.”
https://mg.co.za/article/2019-03-15-00-this-is-why-we-dont-have-water/

Matipane Village - Sodi’s homestead

Journalist, Matome Maila, says Edwin Sodi has built his own “Nkandla” 20kms from his home. He has promised to go there on Saturday and send pictures of the allegedly palatial village home.
Links can be filmed outside Sodi’s home.


Gauteng - Barcelona Primary School

In 2018, this project was awarded to Blackhead Consulting to oversee the project, a contractor would then be managed by Blackhead Consulting. When initially asked in 2022, GDID claimed Sodi’s company was paid a R 2.8 million consulting fee. A year later the DA asked and the GDID says over R 6.5 million was paid for a project still in the “procurement phase”. The school children have been learning in mobile containers and last year, a fed up community burnt down two of the containers demanding a school be built. They have allegedly been waiting for a brick and mortar school structure since 1996.

In 2011, the infrastructure grant to the province provided funding for the school structure to be built - it was to take a year with an estimated completion date of December 2013. It’s unclear what happened.
In 2012, an infrastructure grant to the province for repairs and renovations to be completed in 2012 was green-lighted.
It seems the school is used for comrades to eat.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): A serial tenderpreneur with a penchant for incomplete projects.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Edwin Sodi is a controversial tenderpreneur with questionable links to ANC politicians, including SA’s number two citizen - Paul Mashatile. In the past 10 years, Sodi's companies have been awarded over R 2 billion in tenders and counting across the country North West, Free State, Eastern Cape, Limpopo and Gauteng.

Sodi’s former friend Selloane Lephoi worked with him at Total South Africa where he was in HR recruitment. Ironically, she is now a community activist and one of the incomplete projects she has been raising the alarm on happens to be Sodi’s.
